exposure: timing of birth relative to GGO surgical resection
outcome: radiologic changes in ground-glass opacities (GGOs) (size, solid component)
pathological diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma (e.g., minimally invasive, invasive, preinvasive lesions)
cohort: The study included young female patients with ground-glass opacities (GGOs) suspected for lung adenocarcinoma, divided into groups: those who were pregnant during GGO follow-up, a non-pregnant comparison group, and those who gave birth within two years before GGO surgical resection.
finding: Pregnancy appears to have little impact on the progression or characteristics of ground-glass opacities (GGOs) suspected for lung adenocarcinoma.
